risks.title: IS approval of the named LLD program gates the whole build
risks.description: No Task 3c work may start until MoDOT Information Systems approves the named LLD development program, and the RFP does not say what must accompany the name or what criteria or turnaround the approval uses. If approval is slow or refused, the build, the 4/25/2025 demonstration and everything downstream compress into a shorter window, and the bidder absorbs the idle effort within the fixed price.
risks.justification: The gate is mandatory and sits before the build phase, but the RFP gives no approval criteria or timeline, so the delay depends on facts the RFP does not settle.
risks.mitigation: Ask MoDOT IS for the approval checklist and expected turnaround before the deadline; submit the program name and full technical package immediately after kick-off and hold a pre-approved fallback program in reserve.

risks.title: EPG 236.4.6.2 and the MHTC parameters are not in the RFP
risks.description: The drafting engine must meet MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide Section 236.4.6.2 and generate drafts from 'the MHTC parameters', but neither the guide nor a definition of the parameters is provided. The bidder is therefore pricing an engine against rules it has not read; if the guide turns out to be detailed or the parameters numerous, the rules specification and the engine need unplanned work.
risks.justification: The core technical requirement rests on two documents the RFP does not supply, and the solution assumes both are obtainable at kick-off and captured before build begins.
risks.mitigation: Ask for EPG 236.4.6.2 and the MHTC parameter list with the RFP response; state in the proposal that the price assumes the current published edition and a bounded parameter set, with scope beyond that handled as a change order.

risks.title: The $175,000 cap may not cover the full scope as the bidder reads it
risks.description: The RFP caps the work at $175,000 but does not say whether the cap is all-inclusive across every task, and the task descriptions are described as guidance only. The solution prices the entire fifteen-month scope, including training, reporting and travel, inside the cap; if the true scope is larger than the bidder's reading, the engagement runs at a loss, and if the cap covers only part of the work the price page may be structured wrongly.
risks.justification: A fixed ceiling against an ambiguously bounded scope is the single largest commercial exposure, and the solution's all-inclusive reading is an explicit assumption rather than a stated RFP fact.
risks.mitigation: Ask MoDOT before the deadline whether the cap is all-inclusive and which task descriptions are binding; state in the proposal that the price covers the full scope as described and that additional tasks would require a formal amendment.

risks.title: Oracle 19C vs SQL Server conflict leaves the hosting design and price unsettled
risks.description: The RFP requires on-premise deployments to run on Oracle 19C while also requiring the application to be designed and maintained on the latest supported Microsoft SQL Server, with SQL Server 2016+ only by MoDOT IS Data Service Management approval. The proposed solution commits to Oracle 19C and treats SQL Server as an exception path, so if MoDOT's IS team expects SQL Server (or an approved exception is refused), the data layer, hosting and testing are rebuilt after award. Either way the bidder carries the rework inside a fixed $175,000 ceiling.
risks.justification: The two requirements are directly contradictory and the RFP does not say who chooses the platform; the solution resolves the conflict by assumption rather than by a written clarification.
risks.mitigation: Submit a written question before the 7/17/2024 deadline asking which platform governs and who approves an alternative; state in the proposal that Oracle 19C is the priced baseline and that a SQL Server variant would be a change order.

risks.title: Exhibits A and B are referenced but not in the RFP
risks.description: The RFP requires an Exhibit A sworn affidavit of E-Verify enrolment and no unauthorised alien employment, and an Exhibit B affidavit of lawful presence for sole proprietors and partnerships, but neither exhibit is included in the document. The bidder cannot confirm the exact wording, notarisation or signature requirements, and a defective or missing affidavit is a submission defect that can disqualify the proposal.
risks.justification: Both exhibits are named as mandatory submission items and both are absent from the RFP, so the bidder must reconstruct them from the MoDOT web page before the 8/21/2024 deadline.
risks.mitigation: Download the current Exhibit A and Exhibit B forms from the MoDOT information-for-researchers page at once, confirm with MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov that they are the governing versions, and have the affidavits executed and notarised well before the filing date.

risks.title: Python use may need BRPT approval before the proof of concept
risks.description: The RFP confines Python to ESRI scripts and small one-time uses and requires IS Best Practices Review Team approval for larger use, without defining the threshold. AI/ML work in practice leans heavily on Python, so if the LLD engine needs more Python than the RFP contemplates, the bidder must either re-engineer in C# or wait on a BRPT review that could delay the 4/25/2025 demonstration.
risks.justification: The solution assumes Python stays small and no BRPT review is triggered, but the threshold is undefined and the AI/ML component is the core of the work.
risks.mitigation: State in the proposal that the LLD engine is written in C# with Python limited to ESRI scripts, and ask MoDOT IS to confirm the volume that triggers BRPT review so the design is fixed before build.

risks.title: Unreadable pages 19 and 20 may hide binding requirements
risks.description: Pages 19 and 20 carry almost no extractable text and are dominated by images, so whatever they contain — likely the task list, milestone table or deliverable detail — has not been read. If those pages set obligations the bidder has not priced, the proposal may be non-responsive or the work under-priced.
risks.justification: Two consecutive pages of the RFP could not be parsed and they sit in the section that appears to carry the task and milestone detail the solution relies on.
risks.mitigation: Obtain a readable copy of pages 19 and 20 from MoDOT before the question deadline, re-check the work plan and price against them, and flag any newly found obligation in the proposal.

risks.title: Training and user manual scope is undefined inside a fixed price
risks.description: The RFP requires training and a user manual for Right of Way staff by 7/25/2025 but gives no audience size, number of sessions, format or location, and the solution assumes a small number of virtual or on-site sessions priced within the cap. If MoDOT expects repeated on-site training across districts, the effort and travel cost grow with no price relief.
risks.justification: Training is a mandatory deliverable with an open-ended scope, and the solution's sizing rests on an explicit assumption rather than on anything the RFP states.
risks.mitigation: State the assumed training volume in the proposal (for example two sessions for up to fifteen ROW staff, virtual or at MoDOT premises) and ask MoDOT before the deadline to confirm the expected audience and format.

risks.title: Proof-of-concept property set is not defined, so demonstration effort is unpriced
risks.description: The RFP requires a demonstration of draft LLDs across 'a variety of properties' and a live demonstration on 4/25/2025, but does not say how many properties or which types. The solution assumes roughly 10-20 example properties; a larger or more complex set, or example LLDs delivered late on 12/20/2024, would compress the build and demonstration window.
risks.justification: The demonstration is a fixed-date mandatory deliverable whose effort depends on a property count the RFP does not give, and the example LLDs arrive only four months before the demonstration.
risks.mitigation: State the assumed property count and types in the proposal, ask MoDOT to confirm the demonstration set at kick-off, and prepare a recorded backup demonstration in case live generation fails.

risks.title: Referenced forms and guidelines are outside the RFP and may change the submission
risks.description: The Price Page, Proposal Submission Form, Standard Research Agreement, Publication Guidelines and research summary template are all referenced but not included, and the solution assumes the versions currently posted on the MoDOT website govern. If those documents impose formatting, pricing or contractual terms the bidder has not seen, the proposal may be non-responsive or the post-award contract may carry obligations not priced.
risks.justification: Five governing documents sit outside the RFP and the solution relies on an assumption about which versions apply; the Standard Research Agreement in particular is a post-award contract the bidder has not reviewed.
risks.mitigation: Download every referenced document from the MoDOT information-for-researchers page before drafting, confirm the versions with MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov, and review the Standard Research Agreement for terms that need a price or a stated exception.

risks.title: Data Management Plan due date conflicts with the kick-off-relative deadline
risks.description: One requirement fixes the Data Management Plan at 12/4/2024 while another requires it within two weeks of the 11/15/2024 kick-off, roughly 11/29/2024. The solution plans to the earlier date, which is safe, but if MoDOT treats 12/4/2024 as the contractual milestone and the kick-off slips, the two dates diverge and the bidder risks a missed milestone or a disputed deliverable.
risks.justification: The conflict is real but the solution already plans to the earlier of the two dates, so the exposure is limited to a kick-off slip or a milestone dispute.
risks.mitigation: State in the proposal that the DMP will be delivered within two weeks of kick-off and no later than 12/4/2024, and ask MoDOT to confirm which date governs if the kick-off moves.

risks.title: Interim presentation date conflicts with the mid-point requirement
risks.description: The RFP requires the interim presentation near the project mid-point and also by 9/15/2025, which is roughly ten months into a fifteen-month contract. The solution schedules to 9/15/2025, but if MoDOT later insists on a true mid-point date the presentation, and the reporting cadence around it, must be re-planned.
risks.justification: The solution already resolves the conflict in the safer direction, so the impact is a rescheduling cost rather than a missed obligation.
risks.mitigation: State in the proposal that the interim presentation is delivered by 9/15/2025 and treat that date as the binding one; ask MoDOT to confirm at kick-off.
